p8dd0w: In Spanish, the greeting changes with the time of day and the relationship between the people. This week you learn the basic phrases and the difference between **tú** and **usted**.
am7u1v: To greet anyone at any time, you can say **Hola**. If you want to be more complete or more formal, use the greeting for the time of day: **Buenos días** in the morning, **Buenas tardes** from lunchtime until dark, and **Buenas noches** at night.
jrxu2a: It's very common to combine them: **Hola, buenos días**. After the greeting, you ask about the person: **¿Qué tal?** or **¿Cómo estás?**
gj8l12: To say goodbye: **Adiós**, **Hasta luego** (you're leaving but will be back), **Hasta mañana** and, among friends, **Chao** (in Argentina and Uruguay it's written **chau**).
tfmoki: In Argentina and Uruguay you also hear **Buen día** in the morning.
4phi8: _Día_ is masculine even though it ends in -a.
1elcexx: Who? Yo, tú, usted, él, ella
9vrry0: Subject pronouns say who does the action: **yo** (the person speaking), **tú** (the person you're talking to, informally), **usted** (the person you're talking to, with respect or distance), **él** and **ella** (another person).
m60x43: In Spanish the verb already tells you the person. That's why we normally don't say the pronoun: **Soy Ana** is more natural than _Yo soy Ana_. We use the pronoun to contrast or emphasize: **Yo soy Ana y ella es Lucía.**
1jv2w9: **Tú or usted.** With friends, family, children, and young people, use **tú**. With an older person you don't know, in an office, or with a client, use **usted**. Careful: _usted_ addresses the person in front of you, but the verb is the same as for _él_ or _ella_: **usted es**.
mxt620: In Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, and much of Central America, **vos** is used instead of _tú_: **vos sos**. This week you only need to recognize it.
16tbq5o: With _usted_ the verb is the same as for él or ella: **es**.
1nhd31d: There are three common ways to say your name: **Me llamo Marta**, **Soy Marta** and, a bit more formal, **Mi nombre es Marta**.
10b1t2v: _Llamarse_ always has a small pronoun in front: **me** llamo, **te** llamas, **se** llama. To ask: **¿Cómo te llamas?** (tú) and **¿Cómo se llama?** or **¿Cómo se llama usted?** (usted).
1fpd3cu: When someone introduces themselves, reply **Mucho gusto** or **Encantado** (if you're a man) / **Encantada** (if you're a woman). The other person can answer **Igualmente**.
1suzcph: The verb goes directly after _cómo_; the pronoun is not needed.

dwmz8i: Spanish has only **five vowel sounds**: a, e, i, o, u. They are short, clear, and steady: they sound the same at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end of a word, stressed or unstressed.
1d87dsd: The big difference from English is that in Spanish **vowels are not reduced**. In _chocolate_ you hear all four full vowels: cho-co-la-te. There's no weak vowel like «uh».
rd0dga: They aren't lengthened or glided either: the **o** in _hola_ doesn't end in «u» and the **e** in _mesa_ doesn't end in «i».
eiqz5y: Each vowel is always written with the same letter. The **h** is silent: _hola_ begins with the **o** sound.
